ideas.description: Exploit: combine the near-miss E008 with more epochs. Start from E008, commit cd99006: E004 recipe, 50% of steps at 24 px using bilinear F.interpolate with antialias=False, both shapes compiled and CUDA-graphed in build. Change only the epoch count, from 10 to 11, with the LR schedule rescaled to the new step count so it still anneals fully. First confirm in the commit that E004 and E008 really ran 10 epochs. Timing says they did (E004 8.94 s is about E003's 10-epoch 9.01 s minus cutout), even though E004's description says 8.5.
ideas.expected: Time about 8.2-8.35 s (E008 runs at 0.75 s/epoch at 10 epochs, so 11 epochs is about 8.27 s). That is 7-8% below E004's 8.94 s. Accuracy +0.4 to +0.8 pp over E008's 0.7495, to about 0.753-0.757. If it is feasible this becomes the new best. If accuracy lands at 0.750-0.753, the per-epoch slope near 10-11 epochs is flatter than 0.87 pp/epoch (W4's saturation view, not W2's linear one), and the next step is 11.5 epochs or a smaller low-res fraction rather than more epochs.

ideas.description: Exploit and committee crux: on the E004 recipe (10 epochs, no cutout, LS 0.1, alternating flip, max-autotune plus CUDA graph), change only the random-translate amplitude from 4 px to 2 px. Everything else, including the epoch count, stays fixed. W4 claims translate helps, but every run so far used translate 4, so this tests whether translate 4 still over-regularizes a net that under-fits at 10 epochs, as cutout and LS 0.2 did.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.2 to +0.6 pp over E004's 0.7550, to about 0.757-0.761. Time unchanged within noise (±0.05 s). A gain of 0.4 pp or more banks enough margin to cut about 0.5 epoch (about 0.45 s) in a follow-up. A drop of 0.3 pp or more means translation is the one regularizer worth keeping (supports W4), and translate stays at 4.

ideas.description: Explore: narrow only the middle block. Starting from E004, change the widths from 128/384/576 to 128/256/576, keeping 3 convs per block, and set epochs to 11 with the schedule rescaled. Block 2 at 16x16 is the largest FLOP share (about 0.79 of 1.6 GMACs). Block 3's width is the likeliest source of the capacity the 100-class head needs, and E007/E009 cut both blocks. Estimated conv FLOPs per epoch are about 0.72x those of the wide net.
ideas.expected: Time about 7.7-8.0 s: at 10 epochs E007 got 0.70x the time from 0.57x the FLOPs, so 0.72x FLOPs gives about 0.80x per epoch, times 11 epochs. Accuracy about 0.749-0.756. If it is feasible, it is about 11-14% faster than E004, and block-3 width turns out to be the binding capacity (the E009 ceiling came from narrowing block 3). If accuracy is below 0.749, the width trade-off loses on CIFAR-100 at this budget, and H1.2 should be closed in favour of resolution and epoch levers.

ideas.description: Mechanism test from D003 (C0029/C0031: aliasing from non-antialiased bilinear downsampling, which mismatches the 32 px-fit frozen whitening filters). On E008 (10 epochs, 50% at 24 px), change only the downsampling to F.interpolate(mode='bilinear', antialias=True), done inside the compiled and graphed step. Check in build that both shapes still capture without a recompile in timed train.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.1 to +0.4 pp over E008's 0.7495, to about 0.751-0.754. Time +0.0 to +0.1 s over 7.52 s. A gain of 0.25 pp or more means part of the resize penalty is aliasing, not lost resolution, and the fix carries into the 11-epoch resize line. A gain under 0.15 pp (noise) refutes the aliasing mechanism, and the cost of resizing is all resolution.

ideas.description: On the E004 recipe, change only the label smoothing, from 0.1 to 0.0. This tests whether the leftover smoothing still over-regularizes at 10 epochs on 100 classes, or whether its calibration benefit outweighs that.
ideas.expected: Accuracy change -0.3 to +0.4 pp (direction uncertain); time unchanged. A gain of 0.3 pp or more frees margin to cut epochs. A loss of 0.3 pp or more puts the optimum smoothing between 0.05 and 0.1 and closes the smoothing branch.

ideas.description: Explore whether progress is limited by steps or by samples. On E004, change only the batch size, from 1024 to 768, at equal epochs. Under linear scaling, scale the per-step LR by 768/1024, keep wd per sample as airbench defines it, and tie the schedule to the new step count. Recapture the CUDA graph for the new shape in build and handle the last partial batch the same way as now.
ideas.expected: Steps go from about 49 to 65 per epoch. Time rises 4-10%, to about 9.3-9.8 s. Accuracy +0.2 to +0.7 pp. The run is worth following up only if the gain is above about 0.9 pp per added second, which beats buying epochs. If the gain is under 0.3 pp, the regime is sample-limited, and larger batches (1536) for throughput become the next test.

ideas.description: One decisive test, given that C0015/C0018 contradict it. On E004, add airbench96_faster-style proxy filtering: a 32/64/64 proxy net trained alongside, scoring each 2048-image superbatch, with the main net taking an SGD step only on the top-50% by loss. Main-net epochs are counted in seen-by-main samples, and the main-net step count matches E004. Compile and graph the proxy and the main steps in build.
ideas.expected: The main net's backward passes are halved per raw epoch, but the proxy forward and backward adds about 15-20%. Expected time about 8.0-8.8 s at matched main steps, and accuracy -0.3 to -1.0 pp relative to E004 (hard examples are noisy for 100 classes in an under-fitting regime). Likely infeasible, which would refute H3.1.1 and close H3.1. Feasible and under 8.0 s would be a surprise, worth expanding.

structured_output.summary:
The best feasible run is E004: 0.7550 at 8.94 s. Its description says 8.5 epochs, but its timing and notebook entry point to 10 epochs; check commit 2905511. Its margin over 0.753 is only 0.2 pp.

There were no open queued ideas, so I added seven:
- **Exploit, priority 5:** add epochs to the near-miss E008. Progressive resize at 11 epochs is projected at about 8.27 s and about 0.755.
- **Priority 4:** cut translate from 4 to 2 px to bank accuracy margin. This also tests W4's untested claim that translate helps.
- **Explore, priority 3:**
  - Narrow only block 2, at 11 epochs. E009 points to block 3 as where the capacity limit sits.
  - Test D003's aliasing mechanism with antialiased resizing.
- **Lower priority:**
  - Label smoothing 0.0 (priority 2).
  - Batch 768, to test whether progress is limited by steps or by samples (priority 2).
  - One decisive proxy-filtering test for H3.1.1, which the literature contradicts (priority 1).

Every committee member modelled time as linear in steps and missed the resolution lever (counterexample E008). The 11-epoch resize idea also separates W2's linear 0.9 pp/epoch from W4's saturation view.

Untested and deliberately left out: Muon (H4.2.1, expected refuted) and the whitening ablation (H1.3.1, gives no time gain).
